analysis.investment_thesis: CMS Info Systems is a capital-light duopolist in Indian cash logistics trading at a reasonable 13.45x forward P/E and ~6.3% FCF yield (₹331 Cr FCF / ₹5,244 Cr market cap), suggesting fair but not cheap pricing. The zero promoter stake and EBITDA compression in FY25 (₹717→₹649 Cr despite revenue growth) prevent a full conviction buy.
key_strengths: ROCE of 23.7% and net profit CAGR of 24.6% over 7 years demonstrate genuine economic moat in cash logistics — a regulated, relationship-driven business with high switching costs.
Balance sheet is near-pristine: D/E of 0.10, ₹231 Cr cash, and 5/5 years of positive OCF averaging ~₹354 Cr — this business is self-funding.
Revenue and operating income compounding well (13.9%/23% 7Y CAGR) as banking penetration and ATM infrastructure expansion supports durable demand despite UPI growth.
key_risks: Zero promoter holding is the single biggest governance red flag — Blackstone-promoted PE exits leave no skin-in-the-game owner; minority shareholders lack an aligned insider champion.
Secular displacement risk: India's UPI transaction volumes are growing 40%+ annually — over a 7-10 year horizon, cash-handling volumes face structural headwinds that compress addressable market.
FY25 EBITDA actually contracted YoY (₹717→₹649 Cr, -9.5%) despite 7% revenue growth, signaling margin pressure that the operating income line partially obscures — needs scrutiny.
red_flags: 0% promoter shareholding — no aligned long-term steward; PE-backed businesses with full exits raise second-order governance questions.
EBITDA declined YoY in FY25 while revenue grew — operating leverage is moving in the wrong direction; could reflect depreciation surge from ₹223 Cr new borrowings or rising operational costs.
Finance cost CAGR of 51% over 7 years, though small in absolute terms, signals a trend worth watching if leverage normalizes higher.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
At 15.9x trailing P/E and 9.56x EV/EBITDA, CMS is priced for steady, moderate growth — not perfection. The FCF yield of ~6.3% sits at the lower bound of what I'd call attractive (I prefer 6-8%+), and the forward P/E of 13.45x reflects consensus optimism that margins recover and growth re-accelerates. Second-level question: does the market fully appreciate the EBITDA compression in FY25? That dip — first in the series — may be a one-time capex/depreciation bump (CWIP jumped to ₹142 Cr) or the beginning of margin normalization. The answer materially changes the thesis. At 9.56x EV/EBITDA with 23.7% ROCE, you're not overpaying for quality — but you're not getting a margin of safety either.

The structural moat is real but finite. Cash-in-transit is a licensed, relationship-moat business with high operational complexity — not easily disrupted overnight. India's currency-in-circulation continues growing in absolute terms even as digital payments rise, buying CMS a longer runway than bears suggest. However, the zero-promoter stake demands a higher discount rate. When there's no owner whose net worth depends on the stock price, governance risk rises — buybacks, dividends, and capital allocation discipline can drift. The 60.8% combined FII/DII ownership provides some oversight, but institutional shareholders vote with their feet, not their proxies. I'd want to buy this at ₹270-280 (EV/EBITDA ~8x) to build in a proper margin of safety. At ₹318, the risk/reward is balanced — hold, don't chase.
